diagrams.elements: Higher bucket with water surface, lower basin, clear tube filled by submerging, tube ends in each container; height difference between water surface and outlet marked; arrows for atmospheric pressure (about 101 kPa) pushing down on the bucket surface; direction of flow arrow; second case with outlet level with water surface (no flow)

diagrams.what: Dam cross-section (Masinga-type, 30 m deep) with wall thicker at the bottom (Station B)
diagrams.elements: Dam wall thicker at base, water reservoir 30 m deep; levels marked at 10 m (100 kPa) and 30 m base (300 kPa); pressure arrows longer with depth; P = rho g h = 1,000 x 10 x 30 = 300,000 Pa

diagrams.what: Two-syringe hydraulic jack model matched to Mzee Otieno's jack (Station C)
diagrams.elements: Small piston 5 cm2 (0.0005 m2) with effort 50 N; large piston 100 cm2 (0.01 m2) with load 1,000 N; water-filled connecting tube; pressure 100 kPa transmitted equally; F1/A1 = F2/A2; small piston moves 20 times farther

diagrams.what: Final class model of the knife phenomenon with application panels (students draw on large paper)
diagrams.elements: Sharp and blunt knife edges pressing into a tomato; same force arrows labelled 40 N; contact areas 5 x 10^-6 m2 and 5 x 10^-5 m2; pressures 8 MPa and 0.8 MPa; threshold line at 2 MPa; P = F/A; three small panels: dam (300 kPa at 30 m vs 100 kPa at 10 m), siphon (about 101 kPa, depth difference), jack (50 N gives 1,000 N)

drawn_by_hand_only_note: The Lesson 1 initial model and each learner's Model Comparison strip are free student drawings/writing already on the wall; no slide figure is needed for them.

subject: General Science
title: Economic Importance of Microorganisms: The Dual Nature of the Invisible World

diagrams.what: Dual-Nature Concept Organiser T-chart built live on the board and copied by students
diagrams.elements: Two columns headed 'Beneficial Economic Role' and 'Harmful Economic Role'. Beneficial column rows: Lactobacillus (fermentation of yoghurt/uji), Saccharomyces (leavening bread/mandazi), Rhizobium (nitrogen fixation), Penicillium (antibiotics), methane-producing bacteria (biogas), decomposers (soil fertility). Harmful column: food spoilage/post-harvest losses (ugali, chapati, githeri, sukuma wiki), crop diseases (maize rust, coffee berry disease).

diagrams.what: Students' cumulative personal model of microorganism activity, revised with beneficial and harmful roles
diagrams.elements: Free annotated drawing in notebooks; at least two beneficial roles with microorganism name and Kenyan location (e.g. Rhizobium to bean shamba, Rift Valley), one harmful role linked to ugali/chapati by arrow. No fixed figure for the slide to show.

drawn_by_hand_only_note: Students' own notebook models of microorganism activity are free sketches; the slide only needs to show the T-chart organiser. The Benefit–Harm wall chart, sticky notes and DQB are excluded as poster/board items, and the market and spoiled-food photographs are not diagrams.

diagrams.elements: Regular pentagon with side labelled s = 18 cm on 1 cm² grid; five interior angles marked for protractor measurement (each 108°, sum 540°)

subject: Chemistry

diagrams.what: Periodic table extract showing strontium placed in group 2, period 5 beside Mg and Ca
diagrams.elements: Group 1 and 2 columns with Li, Na, K, Be, Mg, Ca, Sr; Ne and Ar in group 18; atomic numbers and groups/periods labelled; Sr (Z38) highlighted in group 2, period 5

diagrams.what: Electron arrangement (energy-level) diagrams for Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca and Sr to find outer electrons and periods
diagrams.elements: Shells with electrons: Li 2,1; Na 2,8,1; K 2,8,8,1; Mg 2,8,2; Ca 2,8,8,2; Sr 2,8,18,8,2 (5 levels, 2 outer electrons); outer electrons labelled

diagrams.what: Ion formation diagrams showing electron loss/gain to reach noble gas arrangement
diagrams.elements: Na 2,8,1 to Na+ 2,8 (like Ne); Mg to Mg2+; Cl 2,8,7 to Cl- 2,8,8 (like Ar); Sr 2,8,18,8,2 to Sr2+ 2,8,18,8 (krypton-like); charges and electrons transferred labelled

diagrams.what: Revised Class Model poster: chain of reasoning from electron arrangement to formulae, with next-step bonding box
diagrams.elements: Arrows: outer electrons to group; energy levels to period; stability to ion charge; ion charge to formula (SrCl2, SrO, CaCl2, NaCl, Al2O3, KNO3); Sr added in group 2 period 5 with 2,8,18,8,2 and 5s2; 'Next: bonding' box showing atoms sharing electrons to reach a full outer level (octet preview)

drawn_by_hand_only_note: Students' own written predictions, the four-box Final Explanation posters and the DQB strip sorting are free work with no figure required on the slide.

diagrams.what: Reference card: labelled generic plant cell

diagrams.what: Reference card: labelled generic animal cell
diagrams.elements: Animal cell with labels: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, centrioles; no cell wall, no chloroplasts, no large central vacuole

diagrams.elements: Blood smear showing red blood cells (biconcave, no nucleus) and white blood cell (with nucleus); sukuma wiki leaf cells (rectangular, green chloroplasts, large vacuole); labelled cell types for students to point to and link to their model

diagrams.what: Students' revised personal cell diagram distinguishing shared, plant-only, animal-only and specialised features

subject: General Science
title: Writing Chemical Formulae of Common Compounds

diagrams.what: Four-step crossover-valency method worked example board diagram for NaCl, MgO, Al2O3 and CaCO3
diagrams.elements: Symbols side by side with valencies written above (Na+1, Cl-1; Mg2+, O2-; Al3+, O2-; Ca2+, CO3 2-); diagonal crossover arrows dropping the sign to become subscripts; simplification by HCF (Mg2O2 to MgO); bracket rule for radicals; charge-balance check line showing total charge zero

diagrams.elements: NH4 with valency 1+ above it; NO3 with 1- above it; HPO4 with 2- above it; crossover arrows giving NH4NO3 and (NH4)2HPO4; charge-balance check (2 x 1+ = 2+ balances 2-)

subject: General Science

diagrams.what: Cumulative annotated particle model, NaCl section: giant ionic lattice with caption (R1)
diagrams.elements: Regular lattice of alternating Na+ and Cl- ions in fixed positions, ions labelled with charges; caption: fixed lattice positions, no mobile charge carriers, no conductivity; when dissolved or melted ions mobile, conducts

diagrams.what: Cumulative particle model, aluminium section: metallic lattice with sea of delocalised electrons (R2)
diagrams.elements: Rows of fixed positive Al3+ ions; sea of delocalised electrons labelled; layers labelled as able to slide; caption: conducts as solid, malleable

diagrams.what: Cumulative particle model, graphite section: layered hexagonal structure (R3)
diagrams.elements: Flat hexagonal carbon layers, each C bonded to 3 others; one delocalised electron per carbon labelled; weak Van der Waals forces between layers labelled; caption: conducts along layers, layers slide giving pencil marks

diagrams.what: Optional extension mini-diagram of diamond structure for early finishers
diagrams.elements: Each carbon covalently bonded to 4 others in a 3D tetrahedral network; label explaining why no delocalised electrons, so properties differ from graphite

drawn_by_hand_only_note: The Evidence Organiser table, CER posters, DQB columns and the colour-coded Property Prediction Key legend are tables or text frames, not diagrams. Learners' own revisions to the cumulative particle model are hand-drawn in their notebooks.

subject: Essential Mathematics
title: Complementary Angles: Why Does sin 20° Equal cos 70°?

diagrams.what: Right-angled triangle for Wanjiru at the tank tower, with her 37° elevation angle and the other acute angle at the top of the sight line
diagrams.elements: Vertical tower side, horizontal ground side 8 m, hypotenuse as line of sight; right angle marked; 37° at her eye; other acute angle at the top marked and found as 53°

diagrams.what: Right-angled triangle with 35° at A and 55° at B for explaining why sin and cos swap
diagrams.elements: Right angle at C; angle A = 35°, angle B = 55°; side a opposite A, side b opposite B, hypotenuse c; opposite/adjacent labelled relative to A and then relative to B; sin 35° = a/c = cos 55°, cos 35° = b/c = sin 55°

diagrams.what: Class model diagram of the tank problem updated with complementary angles for Wanjiru and Otieno
diagrams.elements: Vertical tower of unknown height; Wanjiru 8 m away with 37° elevation and complement 53° at the top; Otieno 10 m away with 31° and complement 59°; rule sin 37° = cos 53°, cos 37° = sin 53°
